intent.quote: A part from the end-of-turn text showing, I dont think it should be showing anything apart maybe a small minimal status information that indicates a new card was pushed, or that a card was successfully resolved or something like that, and it should be obvious that it is plumb talking. If possible use specific plumb color for this type of indications
intent.readback: plumb shows you very little: a one-line status that also shows progress while plumb works, at most one line in plumb's colour at the end of a turn, and questions. When something needs you it comes as a question through the question tool, or in the browser study room with its diagrams when there is more to study; there are no cards to read and press. The agent gets everything else as text.
will: Keep a one-line status in the status line and a small band above the prompt: the state, the intent in plain words, the counts, and progress with an animation while plumb works.
End a turn with at most one short plumb line, in plumb's colour, saying what changed for you, and nothing when nothing did.
Put to you only questions, each standing alone in your words with its options, consequences, the recommended one and its reason, and no ids.
Use the browser study room for one project's questions that need a diagram or more evidence, and hand your answer back once to the session that raised it.
Have the agent draw a diagram when a question is about structure or flow.
Give the agent everything else as text, on every host.
wont: Cards you read and press, read-back cards, choice cards, and their Confirm, No and Undo buttons.
A panel that walks intents and requirements for you to read (the Obsidian view on request stays).
Questions restated as prose lists, or lists of records at the end of a turn.
Shipping the diagram mod or its skill inside plumb.
A coding agent of the study room's own, for now.
assumptions: The study room opens only when you open it; the plumb line or the agent tells you a question waits there.
'More to study' means a question needing a diagram, or evidence larger than the question tool holds (a long diff, two versions side by side); the agent decides which.
The status says 'awaits you' only when a question waits for you; records the judges are still checking count as plumb's work, not yours.
On hosts without a band (Codex, Pi, Hermes) the status line and plain text carry the status and the plumb line, and questions use that host's own question tool.
The diagram skill comes from the diagram mod's own repository (your 'should be put out of plumb', INT-039, and DEC-044), overriding the old record that had plumb ship it (SR-141).

decisions.question: What does the agent get, and what does the owner see?
decisions.chosen: The agent gets everything as text (brief, ids, stale links, untraced files, warnings, conflicts, answers) whatever the owner sees and on every host; the owner sees the one-line status with progress, at most one plumb line at turn end, and questions through the question tool or the study room. Cards and the full/compact/off setting are retired. The background checks do the work and the band only draws; the session-start hook still records plumb's Python before any slow step so the band always connects, and the two old band tests change their expectation to the brief arriving as text.
alternatives: The agent is told only what blocks it
Keep cards on the panel for the owner, with the full/compact/off setting
No brief text to the agent while the band is up (the old band tests' expectation)

decisions.question: Where does the progress of long plumb work show?
decisions.chosen: Everywhere the owner looks: a bar in the terminal, plain lines in a non-terminal shell, and the same message in the status line and plumb's small band, animated while plumb works (the owner watches the agent, not the shell).
alternatives: Only in the terminal or shell where the command runs

decisions.question: Where do the diagram mod and its skill live?
decisions.chosen: In their own repository (C:/coding/diagram-mod), used beside plumb; plumb's plugin does not ship them, and the study room draws the SVG they produce.
alternatives: A second plugin inside plumb's repository
plumb's plugin ships the architecture-diagram skill

decisions.question: What is the browser study room, and how far does it go?
decisions.chosen: A place to study and answer plumb's questions for one project: the owner reads the evidence and diagrams and answers; the answer goes back to the source session's agent as a follow-up, the way a question-tool answer does. Team coordination and assignments stay with the coding agent's harness; a coding agent of the room's own may come later.
alternatives: An agent workspace with start, steer, pause and resume controls
A project control centre across repositories, agents and people
A separate issue-resolution agent with its own autonomy model
An answer-only browser disconnected from agent follow-up
